name: Quad Clean Energy Supply Chains Initiative and Diversification Program
notes: A leaders' initiative from May 2023 to map and close clean-energy manufacturing gaps in solar PV, electrolysers and batteries. It has joint principles, an AUD 50m Australian-run grant programme (applications from Nov 2024), and reported DFC loans to Tata Power Solar (US$250m) and First Solar India (US$500m). No project list, KPIs or 2025-26 solar-specific activity was found.

name: Section 232 polysilicon action: partner caps, minimum-price equivalence arrangements and onshoring deals
notes: From 4 Dec 2026, deal partners are capped at 15% all-in (UK 10%), and the Commerce Secretary and USTR may change treatment for partners that adopt an equivalent minimum-import-price regime. Commerce monitors partners and stockpiling, and approves company onshoring plans with construction by 20 Jan 2029. No finance line; the incentives are duty exemptions and drawback for partner-sourced polysilicon.

name: EU-India Trade and Technology Council
notes: Ministerial council that met for the third time on 15 Jul 2026 and covers trade, technology and security. No solar-manufacturing pipeline, finance or targets were found in the material reviewed.

name: EU-India Free Trade Agreement
notes: Negotiations concluded on 27 Jan 2026, with tariff cuts on over 96% of EU goods exports; the Commission sought Council authorisation to sign on 11 Sep 2026. The agreement is not yet in force, and its effect on solar tariffs (for example, India's duties on modules and cells) is not established.

name: Lobito Corridor partnership (EU-US MOU with Angola, DRC and Zambia, Oct 2023)
notes: Rebuilds the rail route from the DRC and Zambia Copperbelt (copper, cobalt) to the Atlantic, with Global Gateway (a EUR 116m package) and US PGI finance. It is a logistics corridor with anchor shippers, not an offtake or KPI-based minerals compact, and the US DFC loan is unconfirmed here.

name: US bilateral critical-minerals frameworks and MOUs (Feb 2026 batch) with EXIM finance
notes: Eleven parallel bilateral frameworks were signed on 4 Feb 2026; 10 were signed earlier and 17 more are concluded. They cover pricing cooperation, project development and access to US finance (US$14.8bn in EXIM letters of interest; the Project Vault reserve). The texts and battery-mineral project lists are not published.

name: EU raw-materials strategic partnerships with CRMA strategic projects and RESourceEU finance
notes: The partnerships are political memoranda; their project pipeline is the 13 third-country CRMA Strategic Projects (2025) plus Global Gateway. Finance runs through EIB, Innovation Fund and State aid (more than EUR 2bn under RESourceEU), and the Raw Materials Mechanism matches offtakers. The CRMA 2030 benchmarks are EU-internal, not partnership KPIs.

name: EU-Chile Interim Trade Agreement (in force 1 Feb 2025) and Advanced Framework Agreement
notes: An economy-wide trade agreement, backed by a 2023 raw-materials MoU and Global Gateway work on lithium and copper value chains. It has no named lithium projects or volumes, and the AFA's investment pillar awaits member-state ratification.

name: US-Indonesia Agreement on Reciprocal Trade framework (Jul 2025)
notes: Indonesia committed to remove restrictions on exports of industrial commodities, including critical minerals, to the US. How that squares with the nickel ore export ban is not stated, the 19% tariff rested on IEEPA (struck down in February 2026), and no signed final agreement is confirmed.

name: Minerals Security Partnership and its successor FORGE
notes: Launched as FORGE (Forum on Resource Geostrategic Engagement) at the Feb 2026 Washington ministerial. FORGE replaced the MSP on 4 Feb 2026; the 17 MSP members are reported to have carried over, and Korea chaired it to June 2026. It coordinates project-level work and the reference-price trade-zone idea, with finance through the separate MSP Finance Network. It has no published project list, pooled money or KPIs.

name: MSP Finance Network (ECAs, DFIs and state funds)
notes: Information-sharing and co-financing club set up in Sep 2024 (DFC, EDC, JICA, JBIC, KEXIM, Eksfin and others); finance stays with each institution and there is no published joint pipeline or target. Full membership and any post-FORGE changes are unconfirmed.

name: Agreement on Trade in Critical Minerals (ATCM) negotiations, with the Section 232 mandate and US action plans with Mexico, Japan and the EU
notes: USTR is negotiating a binding plurilateral agreement with phased, mineral-specific, border-adjusted price floors and common standards; Japan, Mexico and the EU joined first via action plans (Feb-Apr 2026). No text is public; scope (reported 5-10 minerals) and price levels are unset, and the Section 232 proclamation keeps tariffs as the fallback.

name: G7 Critical Minerals Action Plan and Critical Minerals Production Alliance
notes: Canada-led alliance announced rounds of named investments and offtakes in Canadian projects (C$6.4bn Oct 2025, C$12.1bn Mar 2026, C$18.5bn in total) with G7 and other partners (Australia, Norway, Luxembourg, Ukraine), plus a standards-based-markets roadmap. Money is mobilised project by project, with no pooled fund; partners in the second round are not named.

name: IEA Critical Minerals Security Programme
notes: Market monitoring, emergency-response exercises (rare earths, Nov 2025) and technical support for national stockpiles, expanded by ministers in Feb 2026; it coordinates rather than funds and holds no joint stockpile.

name: US-Malaysia critical minerals MOU (26 Oct 2025) and reciprocal-trade export commitment
notes: Quarterly working-level meetings to review projects, priority for US investment in Malaysian assets offered for sale, and a price-floor marketplace commitment; no funds obligated. Malaysia pledged not to restrict rare-earth exports to the US but keeps its raw rare-earth export ban, favouring local processing.

name: US-Thailand critical minerals MOU (26 Oct 2025)
notes: Non-binding: first opportunity to invest in Thai assets offered for sale, early tender information, resource mapping, technology transfer and a price-floor marketplace commitment. No named projects or money; implementation activity since signing is not documented.

name: US-Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund (minerals agreement)
notes: Equal US$75m DFC and Ukrainian seed capital, governed by a joint board and committees, targeting three investment decisions by end-2026; critical minerals is one of five sectors. The first investment (Mar 2026) was not a minerals project, and the Dobra lithium award sits outside the fund.

name: US-DRC Strategic Partnership Agreement (Strategic Asset Reserve)
notes: Minerals-for-security deal (Dec 2025): a Strategic Asset Reserve list gives US firms preferential access, reportedly with a right of first offer on exports. A steering committee met in Feb and Nov 2026. The SAR legal framework is not final, and DFC deals are in preparation without published amounts.

name: Quad Critical Minerals Initiative Framework (May 2026)
notes: Up to US$20bn to be mobilised for secure critical-mineral supply chains (secondary source).

name: US-Japan-ROK trilateral supply-chain early warning and critical-minerals dialogue
notes: Camp David (2023) pilot early-warning system, with a Sept 2025 senior-officials commitment to deepen critical-minerals dialogue. No published pipeline or finance; no 2026 trilateral economic-security dialogue statement was found.
